1. A university robotics laboratory runs an automated equipment lending center. Design an ER model and relational schema based on these business specifications. 

a) Borrower: Identified by StudentID. Has a StudentName and an institutional Email. 
-Storing info about students who borrow equipment- STUDENTS
b) Item Category: Identified by CategoryCode (ie. "DRONE", "SENSOR"). Has a descriptive CategoryName 
- Keeping track of equipment categories
c) Equipment Item: Identified by a unique global BarcodeNumber. Each item belongs to exactly one ItemCategory, and an item category must classify at least one item (1:N relationship, total participation on EquipmentItem).
-Keeping track of individual pieces of equipment 
d) Loan Event(LENDS): Students borrow equipment items over time. An equipment item may be borrowed many times over its lifespan, and a student may borrow many items (M:N). Each loan event records a CheckoutDate and an optional ReturnDate. 
-Tracking which students borrowed which equipment item and when - LOAN (Connects students and equipment); LOAN needs two columns for primary key (composite primary key)
e) An equipment item cannot be checked out simultaneously to two students without being returned

Setting up the temporary SQLite database 
```{r}
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)

con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), ":memory:") #creating the database connection stored in con
dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;") #tells SQL to enforce the foreign key relationships defined when tables are created, making sure that foreign keys always reference existing records in the related tables
```

A. STUDENT table - Storing info about each borrower
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TABLE STUDENT (
          StudentID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
          StudentName TEXT NOT NULL,
          Email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
          );
          ")
```

B. ITEM_CATEGORY table - different categories of equipment
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TABLE ITEM_CATEGORY (
          CategoryCode TEXT PRIMARY KEY, --primary key
          CategoryName TEXT NOT NULL --cannot be null
          );
          ")
```

C. EQUIPMENT_ITEM table - individual pieces of equipment
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TABLE EQUIPMENT_ITEM (
          BarcodeNumber TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
          CategoryCode TEXT NOT NULL,
          SerialNumber TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
          PurchaseCost REAL NOT NULL CHECK (PurchaseCost >= 0),
          
          FOREIGN KEY(CategoryCode) --every category code used in this table must exist in ITEM_CATEGORY
          REFERENCES ITEM_CATEGORY(CategoryCode)
          ON DELETE RESTRICT --do not allow a category to be delted if any records in the current table(EQUIPMENT_ITEM) are still using that category 
          );
          ")
```

D. LOAN table- stores each borrowing transaction between a student and equipment item
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TABLE LOAN (
          BarcodeNumber TEXT NOT NULL,
          CheckoutDate TEXT NOT NULL,
          StudentID INTEGER NOT NULL,
          ReturnDate TEXT,
          
          PRIMARY KEY (BarcodeNumber, CheckoutDate), --creating composite primary key
          CHECK(ReturnDate IS NULL OR ReturnDate >= CheckoutDate), --makes sure return date is either empty or occurs after the checkout date for the item
          
          FOREIGN KEY(BarcodeNumber)
          REFERENCES EQUIPMENT_ITEM(BarcodeNumber),
          
          FOREIGN KEY(StudentID)
          REFERENCES STUDENT(StudentID)
          );
          ")

#Preventing simultaneous loans of the same equipmet item 
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TRIGGER prevent_overlapping_loans
          BEFORE INSERT ON LOAN --trigger runs before someone inserts a new row into the loan table 
          FOR EACH ROW --runs for each row being inserted 
          WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM LOAN --Check whether there exists a row in the LOAN table that satisfies the following conditions 
          WHERE BarcodeNumber = NEW.BarcodeNumber --checks whether the existing loan and the new loan involve the same equipment
          AND NEW.CheckoutDate < COALESCE(ReturnDate, '999-12-31') --check whether the new loan starts before the existing loan ends 
          AND CheckoutDate < COALESCE(NEW.ReturnDate, '999-12-31') --check whether existing loan start before the new loan ends
          --both conditions detect overlapping time periods 
          )
          BEGIN 
          SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Equipment item is already checked out'); --if an overlap is found, the new loan is rejected
          END; 
          ")

#Preventing updates to an existing loan in a way that creates an overlapping checkout 
dbExecute(con, "
          CREATE TRIGGER prevent_overlapping_loans_update
          BEFORE UPDATE ON LOAN
          FOR EACH ROW --creates trigger when someone modifies a row in the LOAN table 
          WHEN EXISTS(
          SELECT 1
          FROM LOAN --checking whether at least one row exists in the LOAN table that satisfies the conditions specified next
          WHERE BarcodeNumber = NEW.BarcodeNumber --checking whether another loan involves the same equipment as the updated loan 
          AND NOT(
          BarcodeNumber = OLD.BarcodeNumber
          AND CheckoutDate = OLD.CheckoutDate
          )  --ignore the original row we're currently updating and only check other existing loans so SQL doesn't detect the updating loan as updating with itself 
          AND NEW.CheckoutDate < COALESCE(ReturnDate, '9999-12-31') --checks whether the new loan starts before the existing loan ends 
          AND CheckoutDate < COALESCE(NEW.ReturnDate, '999-12-31')
          ) --checks whether the existing loan starts before the updated loan ends 
          BEGIN 
          SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Equipment item is already checked out');
          END; --if an overlap is found, RAISE(ABORT) stops the update and an error message is displayed. The original loan is left unchanged. 
          ")
```

Insert sample records representing
a. Two students, two categories, and three equipment items
```{r}
#adding 2 students into the STUDENT table 
dbExecute(con, "
          INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES
          (201, 'Amina Sharif', 'asharif@uni.edu'),
          (202, 'Julian Cruz', 'jcuz@uni.edu');
          ")

#Inserting 2 equipment categories
dbExecute(con, "
          INSERT INTO ITEM_CATEGORY VALUES
          ('DRONE', 'Autonomous Quadcopters'),
          ('SENSOR', 'Sensor Units');
          ")

#Inserting 3 equipment items 
dbExecute(con, "
          INSERT INTO EQUIPMENT_ITEM VALUES
          ('BC-001', 'DRONE', 'DN-DJI-11', 1299.00),
          ('BC-002', 'DRONE', 'SN-DJI-22', 1299.00),
          ('BC-003', 'SENSOR', 'SN-VEL-99', 4200.00);
          ")
```


b. Two historical checkout transactions and one currently active checkout (ReturnDate IS NULL)

```{r}
#Inserting 3 records into the LOAN table
dbExecute(con, "
          INSERT INTO LOAN VALUES
          ('BC-001', '2026-10-01', 201, '2026-10-05'), --Student 201 borrowed BC-001 and returned it October 5: Historical transaction
          ('BC-003', '2026-10-12', 201, '2026-10-18'), --Student 201 borrowed BC-003 and returned it October 18: Historical transaction
          ('BC-002', '2026-11-01', 202, NULL); --Student 202 borrowed BC-001 and hasn't returned it yet: Active transaction
          ")

#Checking table contents
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM STUDENT;")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM ITEM_CATEGORY;")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM EQUIPMENT_ITEM;")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM LOAN;")
```

analytical query using appropriate joins to display all active loans, including the student's name, item barcode, category name, and checkout dates.

```{r}
#displaying all active loans 
dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT
           STUDENT.StudentName,
           LOAN.BarcodeNumber,
           ITEM_CATEGORY.CategoryName,
           LOAN.CheckoutDate
           FROM LOAN --start with the loan table since it contains the info about each borrowing transaction, including whether an item has been returned 
           JOIN STUDENT 
           ON LOAN.StudentID = STUDENT.StudentID --to retrieve the student's name 
           JOIN EQUIPMENT_ITEM
           ON LOAN.BarcodeNumber = EQUIPMENT_ITEM.BarcodeNumber --to retrieve info about the equipment item
           JOIN ITEM_CATEGORY
           ON EQUIPMENT_ITEM.CategoryCode = ITEM_CATEGORY.CategoryCode --to retrieve the category name 
           WHERE LOAN.ReturnDate IS NULL; --filters results to include only active loans 
           ")
```
